questions.reason: Actual final cards retain only partial coverage of additive identity, medium effects, and local preassembly. E13 survives as the main comparison for TEA/TEOA under anchored versus composition-normalized recipes, so medium effects are still tested, but the planned broader concentration/amount mapping and explicit necessity/background package from the planned set do not survive as final shortlist cards. E20 probes pre-irradiation donor association with Co-bpy, which addresses additive-specific coordination/preassembly rather than concentration. Planned omission/replacement logic was narrowed: E16 exists as a final card but was only reviewed as revise, not retained, so amine omission and inert-base replacement do not survive as completed final-card coverage. Therefore additive identity and some medium effects are covered, but concentration effects and independent additive-role separation remain visibly unresolved.

Catalyst identity, local environment, component interactions, and stability are the strongest surviving family in the final cards. E19 covers operando cobalt-state comparison under TEA versus TEOA with symmetric no-cobalt backgrounds; E20 tests donor binding/preassembly before illumination; E21 maps deactivation and catalyst persistence; E22 screens donor-linked operando IR/EPR features; E24 checks whether donor-linked effects require bpy or g-C3N4 context; E23 provides a supplementary homogeneous bridge; E05 remains as a near-operando cobalt-state descriptive option. The review explicitly preserves limits: active-species identity remains unresolved, many readouts are descriptive, omission systems are dependence tests rather than mechanistic continuations, and P02 bridging is bounded. Still, this family has multiple retained final cards spanning planned characterization, omission, comparison, and stability designs, so it is covered.

Charge supply and upstream electronic response are covered at the level of steady-state donor-side quenching comparisons in the primary platform and in a supplementary homogeneous bridge. E04 and E07 survive as matched donor quenching/UV-vis characterization in P01, and E09 survives as the P02 quenching transfer. However, the planned stronger kinetic/electronic separation designs were narrowed or not retained as final shortlist coverage: E08 transient reduced-state comparison remained revise, E10 photophysics-to-products correlation remained revise, and E11 donor-radical detection remained revise. Thus the final cards preserve donor substitution and quenching comparison designs but not a completed, stronger chain from charge supply to productive catalytic events. Productive event assignment and causal linkage from electron-supply observables to catalysis remain unresolved.

Substrate interaction and signal assignment survive mainly through descriptive speciation and operando IR-based cards. E15 and E25 probe pre-illumination CO2-associated donor speciation; E26 and E30 provide symmetric operando isotope-sensitive IR/adduct screens; E29 compares TEOA, TEA, and no amine under matched CO2 exposure; E27 bounds CO origin by 13CO2 at the product level. The review repeatedly notes that these signals may reflect bulk amine-CO2 chemistry, catalyst-linked adducts, support-associated species, or mixtures, and that isotope controls bound assignment without proving exact intermediate identity or sequence of subsequent steps. Planned stronger integration against quenching behavior from H05 was not retained as full final coverage, because E28 only became a staged shortlist and remains dependent on optional pilot-qualified substrate-sensitive signals. So substrate interaction and some assignment logic are present, but activation sequence and later-step mechanism remain only partially covered.

Performance, competing products, product origin, and component contributions are well represented in the final shortlist cards. E02 provides matched TEA/TEOA benchmarking with symmetric dark, inert-gas, and no-cobalt controls; E06 and E27 preserve 13CO2 origin checks under both donors; E13 and E17 test whether donor-dependent CO/H2 differences persist or collapse under medium normalization and water-fraction changes; E19 and E21 connect donor-dependent output to cobalt-state/stability trends; E28 adds a stricter matched catalytic comparison with no-cobalt, dark, inert-gas, and optional isotope follow-up. The review correctly keeps limitations visible: origin checks do not explain why donors differ, product data alone do not identify the active species, and some comparisons remain staged or correlative. But the core family asking whether performance/selectivity differences are real, attributable, and CO2-derived is covered by actual final cards.

Independent interventions separating electron supply from other additive roles remain only partly preserved. E13 and E17 survive as medium-normalization and water-fraction interaction tests, and E18 survives as a descriptive bulk-descriptor correlation set; E29 distinguishes TEOA, TEA, and no amine for necessity versus identity at the substrate-signature level. However, the planned more explicit independent interventions were narrowed or did not survive as final covered cards: E16 inert-base replacement/omission remained revise rather than retained, E14 isotope-sensitive proton-coupled operando signatures remained revise, and the planned H05/H03 causal-separation integrations do not survive as completed final-card coverage. Therefore the final cards can show that donor effects depend on medium and that amine presence matters, but they do not fully separate electron donation from proton-management/base/CO2-association roles. This unresolved separation should remain visible.

duplicate_or_complementary_groups.reason: Both are primary-platform donor-side quenching/UV-vis characterization cards in matched P01-like conditions. E04 is framed under H01 as descriptive donor-side quenching comparison in the verified baseline, and E07 under H02 as matched donor quenching in P01. Their retained scientific role substantially overlaps.

Both are isotope-bounded CO-origin checks comparing TEA and TEOA with matched controls. E06 is the cleaner dedicated 13CO2 origin card with donor-matched unlabeled and no-cobalt labeled controls; E27 is a broader matched benchmark with 13CO2 plus inert-gas/dark bounds. They overlap heavily on Q5/Q4 product-origin validation.

Both probe dark, pre-illumination CO2-associated donor speciation under matched P01 medium. E15 emphasizes CO2-equilibrated versus inert solution-state signatures; E25 frames the same idea explicitly around TEA/TEOA/no-amine P01 mixtures before illumination. They are close alternatives for the same descriptive question.

E19 focuses on operando cobalt-state comparison under TEA versus TEOA, whereas E21 adds time-dependent deactivation and catalyst persistence mapped onto product evolution. Together they link state identity trends and stability trends rather than duplicating a single readout.

E20 tests pre-irradiation donor association with Co-bpy formulations, while E24 asks whether donor-linked cobalt-state effects require the full bpy/support assembly through omission comparisons. One localizes preassembly; the other localizes context dependence.

These three retained H03 cards all examine non-redox additive roles from different angles: recipe normalization (E13), water-fraction interaction mapping (E17), and measured bulk descriptor covariation (E18). None alone separates causation, but together they triangulate medium/proton-management involvement.

Both are operando isotope-sensitive IR-based substrate/intermediate screens, but E26 is a donor-symmetric IR assignment card centered on 13CO2/D2O and cobalt-absent references, whereas E30 explicitly pairs operando IR with a preselected cobalt-sensitive method to ask whether donor-specific substrate signals track cobalt dependence.

Both use the supplementary P02 homogeneous bridge, but E09 is a donor-quenching transfer card for Q3 and E23 extends the bridge to cobalt-state-sensitive spectra plus quenching for Q2/Q3. They are linked but not identical.

Both are specialist operando donor-adduct/intermediate screens using IR/EPR-style logic under TEA versus TEOA with symmetric controls. E22 emphasizes IR/EPR donor-adduct screening; E30 emphasizes symmetric cobalt-linked adduct screening with isotope assignment on both donor sides. They are alternative routes to similar H04/H05 discrimination.

E02 is the core matched donor benchmark with symmetric necessity/background controls, while E28 is a later staged matched catalytic discriminator adding quenching and optional substrate-sensitive modules. E28 depends on the same benchmarking logic but extends it rather than replacing it.

overall: Across the actual final cards and review decisions, coverage is uneven but visible. Q2 and Q5 survive strongly: catalyst-state/speciation/stability and validated performance/product-origin/component-contribution questions are supported by multiple retained shortlist cards. Q1, Q3, Q4, and Q6 remain only partial because key planned designs were removed, narrowed, or left at revise rather than surviving as retained final coverage. Most importantly, the planned independent interventions that would separate electron supply from other additive roles did not fully survive: inert-base replacement and stronger isotope/proton-coupled separation designs remained revise, not completed coverage. Likewise, planned stronger electronic-causation designs such as transient reduced-state comparison, photophysics-to-products correlation, and donor-radical detection were not retained as covered final cards, leaving charge-supply-to-productive-event linkage unresolved. Several planned omission and comparison designs did survive in narrowed form: E24 preserves ligand/support omission around donor effects; E29 preserves amine omission versus identity contrast; E13 and E17 preserve comparison designs around normalization and medium crossover; E19/E21 preserve cobalt-state and stability comparisons. But removal or downgrading of E03, E08, E10, E11, E14, and E16 means missing scientific coverage remains visible, especially for concentration dependence, exact signal assignment to subsequent mechanistic steps, and explicit separation of electron donation from base/proton/CO2-association functions. The final set is therefore strongest as a bounded comparative and characterization program, not a completed mechanistic resolution.
